messages:
Alec (SecEng): quick heads-up, pulled today's vuln feed — focusing a short list for triage: CVE-2026-4455 (libcrypto), CVE-2026-4477 (grpc), CVE-2026-4510 (pyyaml). EPSS: 0.62, 0.18, 0.03 respectively. need exploit checks + owners.

cve-bot: automated feed: https://nvd.nist.gov/ids/CVE-2026-4455 | CVSS: 7.8 | EPSS: 0.62 | references: exploitDB link.

Nora: on 4455 — libcrypto used by our token-signing service and the runtime shim. Lina can you confirm runtime image pins? :eyes:

Lina (Infra): checking now, quick grep shows runtime-shim base `openssl 1.1.1k` in 2 images (prod/dedicated). I can build a non-breaking CVE patch image, but need canary schedule.

Samir: CVSS 7.8 -> likely P1. EPSS 0.62 is non-trivial. Is there confirmed remote exploit? any PoC?

Maya (AppSec): NVD refs mention PoC in the wild for certain web stacks. I ran a quick exploitability grep on stack traces and our telemetry shows no 4455-sig activity. still treat as high due to signing use.

Alec (SecEng): agreed P1 for 4455. Owners: Lina for infra patch, Maya to run app-level runtime probe + alert rule. Samir can you do the quick public exploit verification (sandbox)?

Samir: on it. spinning up a sandbox container with vulnerable libcrypto to validate PoC. ETA ~45m.

Nora: note — if patch touches KMS client libs or key wrapping code, we need to coordinate KMS rotation and update audit logging. remember the last KMS rotation playbook (docs/ops/kms-rotation.md) and add a release note for key access.

Lina (Infra): good call. The current runtime-shim doesn't call KMS directly but our token signer service does. I'll open a dependency PR and flag KMS teams for review.

cve-bot: CVE-2026-4477 (grpc) — CVSS: 6.1 | EPSS: 0.18 | no confirmed exploit. Affected in our internal gRPC client wrapper (service mesh).

Maya (AppSec): 4477 looks medium. Impact limited to service-to-service RPCs; fallback path exists. mark P2 unless Samir finds exploitability evidence.

Alec (SecEng): summary + action items: 4455 = P1 (Lina patch + canary, Maya probe + alert, Samir exploit verification), 4477 = P2 (Maya owner), 4510 (pyyaml) = P3 (low EPSS) but add to weekly dependency bump. Also add RBAC check: any hotpatch that updates service manifests needs explicit role approval in prod cluster — @people-ops for temporary RBAC escalation if needed.

Samir: PoC run complete — exploit replicates in sandbox, ability to sign forged tokens demonstrated (low complexity). attaching minimal repro snippet: `python exploit.py --forge-token`. Recommend immediate canary block and token rotation plan.

Lina (Infra): starting hotpatch build now. Canary to staging then one dedicated pool then prod if green. Will annotate deploy with `#cve-2026-4455` and enable verbose audit logging for KMS calls during rollout.

Maya (AppSec): I'll add an alert rule for suspicious token issuance patterns and increase retention for audit logs for 7 days. Also recommend temporary deny on token-issuance endpoints if canary fails.

Alec (SecEng): good. timeline: canary in 2 hours, full rollout in 6 if canary good. I'll update the incident board and escalate to infra oncall if any rollback. tagging this thread in the CVE tracker. :thumbsup:

cve-bot: noted. filing tracker item: https://tracker.internal/cves/2112345678 (auto-created).

Nora: after rollout, let's run a signed-token sweep to ensure no forged tokens accepted. also capture postmortem template link for audit: https://docs.internal/sec/pm-cve.template

Alec (SecEng): agreed. thanks everyone — keep updates in-thread.
